steps.text: Combine jalapeños, lime juice, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper in a blender. Blend until smooth.
Place steak in a shallow pan or large resealable plastic bag. Pour jalapeño marinade over steak and turn to coat. Cover the pan or seal the bag; marinate in the refrigerator for 8 hours to overnight.
Preheat an outdoor grill for high heat and lightly oil the grate.
Remove steak from marinade and cook on the preheated grill to desired doneness, about 5 minutes per side. Discard marinade.

raw_recipe.headline: Jalapeño Steak
raw_recipe.description: This grilled steak tastes sensational after marinating in a blend of jalapeños, lime juice, and garlic.

review.reviewBody: absolutely yummy...i marinated the steak for 2 days...i didn't even blend the ingredients in a blender, i just chopped the jalopenos well and added the steak with them and the garlic and lime in an oversized ziplock. delish:)

This is a great marinade my whole family enjoys. I only use two jalapeños, so while there might not be a lot of heat, it still gives a nice little kick. I’ve also been cutting back on the salt (now add only 1 tsp.) and pepper ( I only add 1/4 tsp.) at the request of my hubby, and they still turn out moist and flavourful.

I cooked this today and my bf loved it. He didn't even use any steak or BBQ sauch,which he normally does with his steak. 

I ended up rubbing the salt, pepper, oregano and a little bit of olive oil onto each side of the steaks. Then I placed it in a bag of cut-up jalapenos and garlic, squeezed two limes into the bag, and let them marinate for 24 hours. 

The steaks were grilled along with the jalapenos. Came out perfect!

one of my favorite marinade recipes now... only differences I did was, I didn't blend it in the blender I just finely chopped my jalapenos and combined all ingredients together, I added a little vegetable oil and marinaded the steak for 8 hours in a shallow baking dish then baked at 350 until desired doneness, turned out absolutely delicious! thank you!

LOVED IT. Used .83 lb hangar steak and halved the marinade, adding a TBSP EVOO. Chickened out of the seeds - home grown jalapenos can vary widely in their heat level. Served with fresh lime wedges to squeeze on the meat. This is a GREAT RECIPE! One of the best on this site. Even DH loved it, and didn't put any steak sauce on it - the ultimate compliment.

This was really delicious! Instead of blending the marinade i just chopped the jalepenos and garlic put them in a ziploc bag with the other ingredients and marinated the steak over night. After grilling i sliced the steak for fajitas and they were soooo good!! I can't wait to make this again, maybe with chicken next time for more fajitas! Thanks for the recipe!
I have limited access to a grill so I roast most meat and I must say that this marinade works great on both pork tenderloin and boneless skinless chicken breasts.

Very good! I had at least 3# of sirloin, so I double the lime, but left all of the other ingredients the same - there was plenty of flavor. I marinated mine for almost 24 hours (did the marinade last night after dinner and threw it in the fridge, easy). I did add a little oil to the marinade about 10 minutes before I grilled it. Turned out lovely - and about as tender as sirloin gets without beating it. Thanks for the recipe!

I loved this marinade! I added a few slices of onion to the mix, used a 1 1/2 lb london broil, and let it sit overnight. I cooked it in a cast-iron grill pan on the stove. I used the meat in a soft taco shell with sour cream and cheese - yum! I had another 1/2 left over that I let marinate for another 24 hours - the flavor was much stronger and better! I sliced this piece up over a salad.

This was a delightful marinade - I removed the seeds from two of the jalapeno peppers and that make it the right amount of heat with lots of delicious flavor! It likely would have been ok to leave the seeds in the other two peppers, but that might have been too much heat for some people. Also, feel free to use the drippings (not the extra marinade!) on the plate after you cook the steak as a yummy gravy on mashed potatoes!

This was a great marinade recipe and I used it with buffalo steaks. Like another reviewer, I didn't use a blender and just finely chopped the ingredients and it worked well, just a little more work. This definitely is one of my favorites now for steaks.
Great recipe and easy to make.
Perfect
The marinade had just the right amount of spice. Very delicious!
Simply delicious! Have made per recipe numerous times. Always produces a perfectly flavorful, tender steak with just the right amount of heat. Great on its own or in fajitas.
Easy recipe and great taste. I used red wine instead of lemon juice, didn’t want the zest.
Very good marinade and I think it would be good as a salsa on nachos or tacos or all things Mexican.Easy to blend up.

This was excellent! Lots of flavor and I didn't even use a grill. I cooked in my cast iron skillet on very high eat, didn't even add oil. I marinated for almost 24 hours. As good as any steak in a restaurant.

I didn't get any heat at all from the Jalapenos. Maybe because I deseeded them? It was still great, but not spicy at all.
This is pretty good. It's a little heavy on the lime and I'll probably use tequila for half of it next time. I used it on elk steak and they are very tender and flavorful.
